title: Trucial States
capsule: The Trucial States were a group of sheikdoms along the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula — including the ancestors of today's UAE emirates — that entered into the General Treaty of Peace with Britain in 1820, pledging to suppress piracy and the maritime slave trade, which gave the coast the name 'Trucial Coast.' Britain signed successive Exclusive Agreements (1892) by which the sheikdoms ceded control of foreign relations in exchange for British protection, formalizing a protectorate relationship that deepened with the establishment of the Trucial Oman Scouts and development councils in the mid-20th century. The dataset's terminal date of 1895 likely corresponds to the Exclusive Agreement of 1892 fully taking effect and the formalization of the protectorate rather than dissolution; the states continued under British oversight until they federated as the United Arab Emirates on 2 December 1971.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The identities and approximate territories of the individual sheikdoms are well attested in British India Office records; precise inland boundaries were undefined and remain uncertain.
